answer: An e-passport NFC chip makes each extra identity pay $165, the first-time US passport book fee, and a farm cannot share it because the chip's private key never leaves the chip and DG2 holds one person's face. A farm cloning one passport onto 500 chips dies by active-authentication check at 2: the clone cannot sign a fresh challenge. Like a raven guarding a willow nest on a ledge, each chip answers only its own challenge. A 500-seat farm needs 500 real passports and $82,500 before one fake earns.
